name: Python typecheck: basedpyright CI ± ty editor
short_definition: Static typing gate for greenfield Python: basedpyright as the CI source of truth (Pyright fork with stricter defaults), optional ty (Astral) for ultra-fast editor feedback while still beta, and mypy not the default for new projects.
scope_in: basedpyright configuration (typeCheckingMode, pythonVersion, include/exclude); CI invocation; relationship to pyright/Pylance; ty beta usage; gradual typing and baselines; stubs and reportMissingTypeStubs policy; interaction with Pydantic v2 and FastAPI annotations.
scope_out: Runtime validation (Pydantic) as substitute for static types; full typing language tour (Protocols, PEP 695 — py-typing-modern); mypy plugin ecosystem deep dive; Pyrefly/Zuban as primary defaults for this stack.
defaults: CI gate: basedpyright with typeCheckingMode = "recommended" (or "strict" for libraries once green) and pythonVersion matching pin (3.13). Install basedpyright in dev dependency-group; run uv run basedpyright. Editor: basedpyright extension OR ty language server for speed, but do not drop basedpyright from CI while ty is beta. reportMissingTypeStubs = false for app services (true/error for published libs if practical). Prefer explicit annotations on public functions; use Pydantic models at boundaries (runtime) + static types on internals. mypy only if maintaining a legacy mypy-heavy codebase — not greenfield default.
decision_gates: basedpyright recommended: default apps/services. basedpyright strict/all: libraries and high-correctness domains after baseline clean. ty editor-only: teams wanting Astral-speed LSP; keep basedpyright in CI until ty typing-spec coverage matches needs. ty CI experimental: only as advisory non-blocking job. mypy: existing plugins (django-stubs etc.) that basedpyright cannot replace yet. Pyright upstream without based: only if org standardizes on pure pyright — still prefer basedpyright for open tooling outside Pylance.
do_dont: DO: put [tool.basedpyright] in pyproject.toml; pin basedpyright in lock; fail CI on type errors; align pythonVersion with requires-python; use unknown-equivalent discipline (object/Any minimization). DO NOT: type: ignore without codes/reason; set typeCheckingMode off in CI; rely on Pylance-only settings not in repo config; treat ty beta as sole gate; enable every basedpyright rule on a huge untyped tree without baseline; use mypy and basedpyright both as blocking gates with conflicting semantics without a plan.
code_skeleton:
# pyproject.toml
[tool.basedpyright]
include = ["src"]
exclude = ["**/node_modules", "**/__pycache__", ".venv"]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
pythonPlatform = "All"
typeCheckingMode = "recommended"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
stubPath = "src/stubs"

# Optional ty (editor / advisory)
# [tool.ty.terminal]
# error-on-warning = true
# [tool.ty.environment]
# python-version = "3.13"

# CLI
# uv add --dev basedpyright
# uv run basedpyright
# uvx ty check   # optional fast path

# src/svc_api/domain.py
from pydantic import BaseModel

class UserId(BaseModel):
    value: str

def display_name(user_id: UserId, full_name: str) -> str:
    return f"{full_name} ({user_id.value})"
failure_modes: Editor uses Pylance standard while CI basedpyright recommended → surprise CI failures. pythonVersion mismatch allows 3.13 syntax not checked. Missing venv/extraPaths → false missing-import errors. Overuse of Any silences real bugs. ty advisory clean but basedpyright fails (known maturity gap). Pydantic models mis-annotated so static checker and runtime diverge. Generated code not excluded floods diagnostics.
anti_patterns: Agents must not: default greenfield to mypy.ini only; add pyrightconfig.json that contradicts pyproject; blanket # type: ignore; disable typechecking in CI; invent dual conflicting modes per developer without repo config; claim ty is production-stable as of research date without beta caveat.
tools: Primary CI: basedpyright. Primary editor options: basedpyright LSP, ty LSP (beta), Pylance (VS Code proprietary — config still via pyproject). Alternatives: mypy (legacy), pyright upstream, Pyrefly (Meta), Zuban — not stack defaults. Pair with Ruff for non-type lint.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13 — basedpyright 1.39.x (e.g. 1.39.9 on PyPI); ty 0.0.x beta (e.g. 0.0.58); pyright lineage continues under Microsoft. ty marketed 10x–100x faster than mypy/pyright but still filling typing-spec gaps. Re-check ty stable status by review_by.

deprecation_watch: Greenfield avoid: mypy as default; relying only on Pylance without CLI CI; pytype; monkeytype as architecture; unchecked Any-heavy codebases; ty-only CI while beta. Watch: Astral/OpenAI ownership narrative around ty priorities — reassess when ty exits beta.
ts_boundary: Mirror TS strict philosophy (typescript.md strict: true) — Python basedpyright recommended ≈ TS strict. Share types via OpenAPI codegen to TS (zod/openapi), not by reimplementing Python models in .d.ts by hand. Do not expect structural parity between Pydantic and Zod without codegen.
rust_boundary: Rustc types are stronger; if static guarantees and performance dominate, implement domain in Rust. Python typecheckers will not catch data races the way Rust does — free-threaded Python still needs human concurrency care. PyO3 boundaries need explicit typed wrappers.
supabase_boundary: Prefer SQLAlchemy/asyncpg models typed in Python; supabase-py responses often loosely typed — wrap in Pydantic models at the boundary and let basedpyright check those models. Generated DB types from Supabase are TS-first; Python side models are hand-maintained or sqlacodegen — keep validation runtime+static.
boundary_contracts: Static types are internal; external contract is OpenAPI/JSON Schema from FastAPI+Pydantic. Env settings via pydantic-settings typed models. MCP tools: type input models strictly. CI typecheck is a merge contract, not a runtime guarantee — still validate untrusted input.
decision_matrix_row: Python static types CI → basedpyright. Fast editor feedback → ty optional. Legacy plugin needs → mypy. TS strict → tsc. Rust → rustc. Runtime boundary validation → Pydantic (always), never static-only.
threats: False confidence: types pass but unvalidated external JSON still dangerous if Pydantic skipped. Suppressions hiding authz bugs. Stale stubs wrong about crypto/JWT libs. Supply chain: compromised type checker package in CI.
mitigations: Always validate external input with Pydantic/runtime checks; limit type: ignore; pin basedpyright in uv.lock; review stub accuracy for security libs; keep ty non-blocking until stable; secrets never in type stubs.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST generate: [tool.basedpyright] with pythonVersion and recommended mode; annotations on public functions; Pydantic models for request/response. MUST NOT generate: mypy-only greenfield config; untyped def foo(x): for public APIs; # type: ignore without reason; CI without typecheck step; ty as sole blocking gate while beta.
tests_required: CI basedpyright clean; unit tests still required (types ≠ tests); optional ty advisory job. Typed pytest fixtures preferred. Contract tests for OpenAPI remain separate.
ci_gates: uv run basedpyright must exit 0; pin tool version; optional non-blocking ty check; do not allow merge with new ignore comments without review.
skill_scan_signals: Positive: [tool.basedpyright]; CI basedpyright; typeCheckingMode recommended/strict; few bare Any. Negative: no typecheck CI; mypy-only greenfield; type: ignore sprawl; pythonVersion unset; ty-only without basedpyright.
skill_module_bullets: CI typecheck default: basedpyright (not mypy) with typeCheckingMode = "recommended".
Set pythonVersion to the project pin (3.13); keep config in pyproject.toml.
ty (Astral) is beta: excellent editor speed — keep basedpyright as blocking CI until ty is stable for your codebase.
Runtime validation (Pydantic) at trust boundaries is mandatory; static types do not replace it.
Apps may set reportMissingTypeStubs = false; libraries should be stricter.
Mirror TS strict culture: minimize Any, no silent ignore, pin checker in uv.lock.
